tasks.title: P1: Enforce admin role on user routes server-side
tasks.description: Today any logged-in user can create, promote or delete users, including the admin. Enforce roles in the API.
tasks.details:
server/index.js: authenticateToken only at GET/POST /api/users, PUT/DELETE /api/users/:id (~lines 112, 217, 271, 304). Add requireAdmin middleware. Rules: only admin lists/creates/updates/deletes users; a user may read and change only their own password; nobody can change their own role; the last admin cannot be deleted or demoted. Take the role from the verified token, never from the request body.

[2026-10-29T20:41:44-04:00] plan: server/index.js only (+ new server/test/users-roles.test.js). Add requireAdmin (re-reads users.json so a demoted/deactivated admin loses access immediately; token role not trusted alone). GET/POST /api/users, DELETE: admin only. GET/PUT /api/users/:id: admin or self; self may change only password; admin may change fullName/role/isActive/password via allow-list (no passwordHash/id mass-assignment); nobody changes own role/isActive; last active admin cannot be deleted/demoted/deactivated; self-delete refused (UI already says 'Cannot delete yourself'). Frontend only fetches users when admin, so no UI breakage. Note: useAuth still calls init-admin on load -> task 4 must remove that call.

[2026-10-29T20:44:16-04:00] result: requireAdmin + self/admin rules implemented; 6 new API tests (16 total) pass. Same tests against the OLD index.js: failures (confirms they test the fix). Decisions: role verified against stored user, not token alone; admin can't change own role/isActive; self-delete refused. Drift check: only server/index.js + new test; no frontend change needed.
tasks.testStrategy: API tests: operator token gets 403 on create/promote/delete user and on self-promotion; admin succeeds; deleting the last admin is refused

tasks.title: P1: Require JWT_SECRET at startup
tasks.description: The server falls back to a public default secret, which allows forged admin tokens.
tasks.details:
server/index.js line 17. Exit with a clear error if JWT_SECRET is missing or shorter than 32 chars. Update .env.example and the Docker/compose docs. DEPLOY RISK: the API will refuse to start on the VPS if JWT_SECRET is not set there. Ask the owner to confirm (open question in PRD) before this reaches production, and note that changing the secret logs everyone out.

[2026-10-29T20:00:33-04:00] plan: new server/config.js exporting resolveJwtSecret(env) (throws on missing/blank, known placeholder incl. the old default and the value in server/.env.example, or <32 chars). server/index.js L17 calls it at startup and exits 1 with the message. Update server/.env.example (blank value + openssl rand -hex 48 hint), comment in docker-compose.yml, one note in SERVER_SETUP_GUIDE.md. Tests: unit cases for resolveJwtSecret plus child-process tests: no secret -> exit 1, old default -> exit 1, valid secret -> actually listens (also proves the NODE_ENV listen guard from task 1 does not affect production start). DEPLOY RISK stays open: VPS server/.env may be missing or hold the old placeholder. Do not merge/deploy until owner has set a real value.

[2026-10-29T20:02:28-04:00] done: server/config.js resolveJwtSecret (rejects missing/blank, public placeholders incl. old default, <32 chars); index.js exits 1 with a fix message; .env.example now blank + instructions (also local-dev hint, since the server has no dotenv); docker-compose.yml comment. Tests: 8 new in server/test/jwt-secret.test.js incl. real child-process start (no secret -> exit 1, old default -> exit 1, valid secret -> listens). 10/10 server tests, root tests and tsc pass. Not verified: a Docker image build/run (no Docker here). Skipped SERVER_SETUP_GUIDE.md on purpose: it documents the obsolete /var/www setup (Phase 8). Drift check: matched task and PRD. DEPLOY GATE: do not deploy until VPS server/.env has a real JWT_SECRET; if it was copied from the old .env.example it holds the rejected placeholder.
tasks.testStrategy: Starting the server without JWT_SECRET exits non-zero with a message; with a valid secret the existing API tests pass

tasks.title: P1: Login rate limit, password rules, CORS allow-list
tasks.description: Audit: 51 bad logins in a row all just 401; passwords need only 3 characters; CORS is open.
tasks.details:
server/index.js: cors() at line 26, login route ~line 199. Add express-rate-limit on /api/login (and user creation), minimum password length 10 on create/change, CORS restricted to an origin list from env (default same-origin).

[2026-10-29T20:47:04-04:00] plan: NO new dependency (task text suggested express-rate-limit but PRD didn't choose a library; adding deps needs user OK) -> own small in-memory limiter server/login-limiter.js: failed logins only, 10 fails/15min per username and 50/15min per IP -> 429 with Retry-After, success clears username bucket. trust proxy for private ranges so req.ip is the real client behind Traefik/nginx (nginx-docker.conf untouched; if IP resolves to the proxy the per-username bucket still protects accounts). Password min 10 on create + change (existing weak passwords still log in; only new ones enforced); align reset-admin.js (8->10) and UI check (3->10). CORS: CORS_ORIGINS env list, default none => no CORS headers (same-origin via nginx/vite proxy keeps working). Update my earlier tests' short passwords. Not doing: separate limit on user creation (already admin-only after task 3).

[2026-10-29T20:49:11-04:00] result: login-limiter.js (own code, no new dep), 429+Retry-After after 10 fails/user or 50/IP, min password 10 on create/change (existing weak passwords can still log in), CORS_ORIGINS allow-list default none, reset-admin/readme/UI aligned to 10. 24 server tests pass, tsc ok. PRE-DEPLOY NOTE: nginx-docker.conf sets X-Real-IP but not X-Forwarded-For; per-IP bucket may see the proxy IP (50/15min shared) until Phase 8 fixes nginx; per-username bucket is unaffected. Lockout is per account so someone can deliberately lock a user for 15 min (accepted tradeoff). Drift check: ok.
